 Judgment

The Insurer is in appeal in MFA No.103227/2017 questioning the saddling of entire liability as well as quantum of compensation, whereas the claimants are in cross-objection in MFA Crob No.100022/2021 praying for enhancement of compensation.

2. The above appeal and cross-objection are filed against judgment and award dated 25.04.2017 passed in MVC No.264/2016 on the file of learned I Addl. MACT, Karwar (for short, 'Tribunal').
3.

The claimants, wife, son and mother of deceased Narayanappa Nagappayya Hebbar, filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 seeking compensation for the accidental death of Narayanappa Nagappayya Hebbar that took place on 6.12.2015 involving Tata Indica Car bearing registration No.KA-27/A-1061 and VRL Bus bearing registration No.KA-25/D-4797.

It is stated that the deceased was a government servant working as FDA in District Treasury Office,
Karwar, drawing salary of Rs.33,445/- per month, aged about 54 years as on the date of the accident.
NC: 2024:KHC-D:1042-DB C/W MFA.CROB No.100022 of 2021 4.
In response to notice, respondents No.1, 2 and 4 entered appearance through their learned counsel.

Respondent No.1 filed statement of objections denying the entire claim petition averments and contended that offending vehicle i.e. VRL Bus bearing registration No.KA-25/D-4797 was insured with respondent No.2/insurer as on the date of accident.
Respondent No.2/Insurance Company filed written statement denying the claim petition averments.

It was contended that driver of the offending vehicle was not having valid and effective driving license as on the date of the accident.

sentences.text: Before the Tribunal, claimant No.1-wife of the deceased examined herself as PW1 apart from marking the documents as Exs.P1 to P93.
The respondents did not examine any witness but marked insurance policy as Ex.R1.

The Tribunal based on the material on record awarded a total compensation of Rs.30,36,804/- with interest at 7% per annum from the date of petition till realization on the following heads:
 Loss of dependency Rs.29,16,804/-
 Loss of consortium Rs. 30,000/-
 Loss of estate Rs. 35,000/-
 Funeral expenses Rs. 25,000/-
 Loss of love & affection Rs. 30,000/-
NC: 2024:KHC-D:1042-DB  C/W MFA.CROB No.100022 of 2021 6.
Heard the learned counsel Sri. N.R. Kuppelur for insurance company as well as learned counsel Sri.Shivakumar S Badawadagi for the claimants and perused the appeal papers along with original records.

7. Sri.N.R.Kuppelur, learned counsel appearing for the Insurance Company in support of his appeal would submit that since the deceased was a government servant and aged 54 years, the Tribunal ought to have adopted split multiplier.

He further submits that the deceased was to retire on attaining the age of 60 years and he would not have earned salary, which he was earning during his service; and he would have received pension, as such, the Tribunal ought to have applied split multiplier while determining compensation on the head of loss of dependency.

It is his submission that salary drawn should have been taken upto his retirement and after the date of his retirement,
pension of the deceased ought to be taken for determining loss of dependency.
Therefore, he submits that the claimants would be entitled for compensation on applying split multiplier.

It is further contended that the Tribunal committed an error in not deducting income tax at the rate of 10% and professional tax of Rs.200/- per month while computing loss of NC:
2024:KHC-D:1042-DB C/W MFA.CROB No.100022 of 2021 dependency.
He further submits that the Tribunal committed an error in awarding 7% interest on the compensation amount.
It is his submission that normally, this Court grants rate of interest at 6% per annum on the compensation amount taking note of Bank rate of interest.
8. Nextly, learned counsel Sri.N.R. Kuppelur would vehemently contend that the Tribunal failed to consider contributory negligence and saddled entire liability on the appellant/insurance company.
He would further submit that the accident in question occurred due to negligence of both drivers of Indica car as well as VRL bus.
Thus, he prays for modifying the judgment and award of the Tribunal by allowing the appeal filed by the Insurer.

sentences.text: Per contra, Sri.Shivakumar S Badawadagi, learned counsel for the claimants in support of his cross-objection submits that the Tribunal failed to award any compensation on the head of future prospects, which the claimants would be entitled to 15%, since the deceased was a government employee having permanent employment.

He would further submit that the deceased was aged 54 years and in terms of decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance NC:
2024:KHC-D:1042-DB C/W MFA.CROB No.100022 of 2021 Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi &
Others1, if the deceased was in permanent employment and aged between 50- 60 years, the claimants would be entitled for addition of 15% of the assessed income towards future prospects.

Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation Ltd.2, to contend that method of determination of compensation applying two multipliers is clearly erroneous and run counter to the judgment in Pranay Sethi(supra).

sentences.text: It is his submission that the Hon'ble Apex Court has made it clear in Valli (supra) that multiplier has to be applied based on the age of the deceased and applying split multiplier is clearly erroneous.

Further, learned counsel would submit claimants would be entitled to Rs.40,000/- each towards spousal consortium, parental consortium and filial consortium as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Magma General (2017) 16 SCC 680 (2022) 5 SCC 107 NC:

sentences.text: Thus, he prays for allowing the cross-objection filed by the claimants and to dismiss the appeal filed by the insurer.

11. Having heard the learned counsel for both the parties and on perusal of the appeal papers along with original records, the following points would arise for consideration:
i) Whether the split multiplier would be applicable as contended by the insurer?
ii) Whether the Tribunal was justified in saddling entire liability on the appellant/insurance company?
iii) Whether the claimants would be entitled for adding future prospects at 15% of the assessed income as contended by the claimants?

Point No.(i) is answered in the negative and point No.(ii) and (iii) are answered in the affirmative for the following reasons:
a) The occurrence of the accident on 6.12.2015 and resultant death of Narayanappa Nagappayya Hebbar involving Tata Indica Car bearing registration No.KA-27/A- 1061 and VRL Bus bearing registration No.KA-25/D-4797 is 2018 ACJ 2782 - 10 - Smt. Nagratna Narayan Hebbar vs The Md Vrl Logistic Ltd

It is also not in dispute that as on the date of accident, the deceased was working as FDA in District Treasury Office, Karwar and aged 54 years.

It is the contention of the insurer that since the deceased was a government servant and had left with four years of service, split multiplier has to be adopted while determining the loss of dependency, as the deceased would not get same salary on attaining the age of superannuation and the deceased would have received only pension, which would be 50%
of his last pay drawn.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in Valli (supra) was considering the question of application of split multiplier and while answering the said question, the Hon'ble Apex Court at paragraph-9 has observed as follows:
9.

Thus, we find that the method of determining of compensation applying two multipliers is clearly erroneous and run counter to the judgment of this Court in Pranay Sethi, affirming the judgment in Sarla Verma.
Since the deceased was 54 years of age on the date of incident, therefore, the suitable multiplier would be 11 as per judgment of this Court in Sarla Verma approved by this Court in Pranay Sethi.
(emphasis supplied)

b) A reading of the above paragraph would make it clear that the Hon'ble Apex Court has held that applying - 11 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:1042-DB C/W MFA.CROB No.100022 of 2021 two multipliers is clearly erroneous and run counter to the judgment in Pranay Sethi (supra).
Therefore, multiplier applied by the Tribunal is proper and correct and contention of the insurer with regard to application of split multiplier is liable to be rejected and it is rejected.
c) It is the contention of the insurer that the Tribunal failed to consider contributory negligence.
On perusal of the records, we are of the view that the Tribunal rightly saddled liability on the appellant/insurance company.

The deceased was travelling along with 1st claimant in Indica Car bearing registration No.KA-27/A-1061 and was proceeding from Hangal to Manipal, whereas the offending vehicle VRL bus was coming in opposite direction from Murudeshwar towards Honnavar.
It is stated that the said VRL bus came in high speed in a rash and negligent manner and caused accident.
Admittedly, the charge sheet is filed against driver of VRL bus.
Moreover, driver of the bus or any other eye-witness is not examined to establish the contention of contributory negligence.

On the other hand, material evidence on record would establish that the accident had occurred solely due to rash and negligent - 12 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:1042-DB C/W MFA.CROB No.100022 of 2021 driving of driver of VRL bus.
Taking note of all these aspects into consideration, we are not inclined to interfere with the finding recorded by the Tribunal insofar as contributory negligence is concerned.

Accordingly, we reject the Smt. Nagratna Narayan Hebbar vs The Md Vrl Logistic Ltd on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191617842/
7 said contention.
d) It is the contention of the claimants that the Tribunal failed to award any compensation towards future prospects, which the claimants would be entitled to at 15% of the assessed income.

sentences.text: Admittedly, the deceased was a government servant and drawing a salary of Rs.33,445/- per month.

In terms of decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Pranay Sethi (supra), if the deceased was in permanent employment and aged between 50-60 years, the claimants would be entitled for adding 15% of the assessed income towards future prospects.
Hence, in the instant case, the claimants would be entitled to addition of 15% of the assessed income towards future prospects.
From the assessed income of Rs.33,445/- per month, professional tax of Rs.200/- per month and admissible income tax has to be deducted to reckon the net salary of the deceased.

On perusal of the records,
the claimants - 13 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:1042-DB C/W MFA.CROB No.100022 of 2021 have produced salary slip of the deceased marked at Ex.P82, but no income tax returns are filed.

Taking note of Ex.P82-Salary Slip for the month of November, 2015, the deceased would not be liable to pay income tax as per following computation:
GROSS SALARY (Rs.33,445 x 12) 4,01,340 Less: Professional Tax (200 x 12) 2,400 GPF (11000x12) 132000 GIS (120x12) 1440 KGID (645x12) 7740
Total Deductions 1,44,108 2,57,232

Total Taxable Income (-250000) 7232 Tax payable as per slab (10%) 723.2 Less: Income tax rebate u/s 87A 2500 Tax payable on total income Nil Add: Education Cess @ 2% + SHEC @ 1% -
 TOTAL TAX PAYABLE Nil  e) In view of the above calculation, the deceased was not liable to pay any income tax.
Hence, the only admissible deduction, which is to be deducted from the assessed income is, professional tax of Rs.200/- per month.

After deducting a sum of Rs.200/- per month as professional tax from the assessed income of Rs.33,445/-
per month, the net income of the deceased would be - 14 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:1042-DB C/W MFA.CROB No.100022 of 2021 Rs.33,245/- per month.
There is no dispute with regard to applicability of multiplier of 11 and deduction of 1/3rd towards personal and living expenses of the deceased.

Accordingly, the claimants would be entitled to modified compensation on the head of loss of dependency as under:
Rs.33,245(income) + 15%(future prospects) x 12(months) x 11 (multiplier) x 2/3 (deduction)=Rs.33,64,394/-
12.

Further, the claimants being wife, son and mother of the deceased would be entitled to Rs.40,000/- each towards spousal, parental and filial consortium respectively as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Magma General Insurance Company Limited (supra).
Further, the claimants would be entitled to Rs.15,000/- towards loss of estate and Rs.15,000/- towards funeral expenses and transportation of dead body.

Thus, the claimants would be entitled for modified compensation on the following heads:

Particulars

1. Loss of dependency Rs.33,64,494/-
2. Loss of estate & Funeral expenses Rs. 30,000/-
3. Spousal & Parental Consortium Rs. 1,20,000/-
(Rs.40,000/- each to claimants 1 to 3) Total Rs.35,14,394/-
- 15 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:1042-DB C/W MFA.CROB No.100022 of 2021 13.
Thus, the claimants would be entitled to total compensation of Rs.35,14,394/- as against Rs.30,36,804/- awarded by the Tribunal.
14. The Tribunal while awarding compensation granted rate of interest at 7% per annum.

Taking note of the present rate of Bank interest, we are inclined to reduce the rate of interest on the compensation amount from 7% awarded by the Tribunal to 6% per annum.
15.

Hence, we pass the following:
ORDER a) The appeal as well as cross-objection are allowed in part.
b) The impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal is modified to the extent that the claimants are entitled to total compensation of Rs.35,14,394/- as against Rs.30,36,804/- awarded by the Tribunal.
c) The entire compensation amount will bear interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till date of realization.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The claimants, wife, son and mother of deceased Narayanappa Nagappayya Hebbar, filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 seeking compensation for the accidental death of Narayanappa Nagappayya Hebbar that took place on 6.12.2015 involving Tata Indica Car bearing registration No.KA-27/A-1061 and VRL Bus bearing registration No.KA-25/D-4797.
Respondent No.1 filed statement of objections denying the entire claim petition averments and contended that offending vehicle i.e. VRL Bus bearing registration No.KA-25/D-4797 was insured with respondent No.2/insurer as on the date of accident.
Respondent No.2/Insurance Company filed written statement denying the claim petition averments.
It was contended that driver of the offending vehicle was not having valid and effective driving license as on the date of the accident.

opennyai_summary.issue:
11. Having heard the learned counsel for both the parties and on perusal of the appeal papers along with original records, the following points would arise for consideration:
i) Whether the split multiplier would be applicable as contended by the insurer?
ii) Whether the Tribunal was justified in saddling entire liability on the appellant/insurance company?
iii) Whether the claimants would be entitled for adding future prospects at 15% of the assessed income as contended by the claimants?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
On perusal of the records, we are of the view that the Tribunal rightly saddled liability on the appellant/insurance company.
The deceased was travelling along with 1st claimant in Indica Car bearing registration No.KA-27/A-1061 and was proceeding from Hangal to Manipal, whereas the offending vehicle VRL bus was coming in opposite direction from Murudeshwar towards Honnavar.
Admittedly, the charge sheet is filed against driver of VRL bus.
Moreover, driver of the bus or any other eye-witness is not examined to establish the contention of contributory negligence.
On the other hand, material evidence on record would establish that the accident had occurred solely due to rash and negligent - 12 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:1042-DB C/W MFA.CROB No.100022 of 2021 driving of driver of VRL bus.
Admittedly, the deceased was a government servant and drawing a salary of Rs.33,445/- per month.
On perusal of the records,
the claimants - 13 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:1042-DB C/W MFA.CROB No.100022 of 2021 have produced salary slip of the deceased marked at Ex.P82, but no income tax returns are filed.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Hence, in the instant case, the claimants would be entitled to addition of 15% of the assessed income towards future prospects.
From the assessed income of Rs.33,445/- per month, professional tax of Rs.200/- per month and admissible income tax has to be deducted to reckon the net salary of the deceased.
Taking note of Ex.P82-Salary Slip for the month of November, 2015, the deceased would not be liable to pay income tax as per following computation:
GROSS SALARY (Rs.33,445 x 12) 4,01,340 Less: Professional Tax (200 x 12) 2,400 GPF (11000x12) 132000 GIS (120x12) 1440 KGID (645x12) 7740
Total Deductions 1,44,108 2,57,232
Hence, the only admissible deduction, which is to be deducted from the assessed income is, professional tax of Rs.200/- per month.
After deducting a sum of Rs.200/- per month as professional tax from the assessed income of Rs.33,445/-
per month, the net income of the deceased would be - 14 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:1042-DB C/W MFA.CROB No.100022 of 2021 Rs.33,245/- per month.
There is no dispute with regard to applicability of multiplier of 11 and deduction of 1/3rd towards personal and living expenses of the deceased.
Accordingly, the claimants would be entitled to modified compensation on the head of loss of dependency as under:
Rs.33,245(income) + 15%(future prospects) x 12(months) x 11 (multiplier) x 2/3 (deduction)=Rs.33,64,394/-
12.
Further, the claimants being wife, son and mother of the deceased would be entitled to Rs.40,000/- each towards spousal, parental and filial consortium respectively as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Magma General Insurance Company Limited (supra).
Further, the claimants would be entitled to Rs.15,000/- towards loss of estate and Rs.15,000/- towards funeral expenses and transportation of dead body.
Thus, the claimants would be entitled for modified compensation on the following heads:
Sl.No.
Particulars
Amount
1. Loss of dependency Rs.33,64,494/-
2. Loss of estate & Funeral expenses Rs. 30,000/-
3. Spousal & Parental Consortium Rs. 1,20,000/-
(Rs.40,000/- each to claimants 1 to 3) Total Rs.35,14,394/-
- 15 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:1042-DB C/W MFA.CROB No.100022 of 2021 13.
Thus, the claimants would be entitled to total compensation of Rs.35,14,394/- as against Rs.30,36,804/- awarded by the Tribunal.
14. The Tribunal while awarding compensation granted rate of interest at 7% per annum.
Taking note of the present rate of Bank interest, we are inclined to reduce the rate of interest on the compensation amount from 7% awarded by the Tribunal to 6% per annum.
15.
Hence, we pass the following:
ORDER a) The appeal as well as cross-objection are allowed in part.
b) The impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal is modified to the extent that the claimants are entitled to total compensation of Rs.35,14,394/- as against Rs.30,36,804/- awarded by the Tribunal.
c) The entire compensation amount will bear interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till date of realization.

9
d) The appellant-Insurer shall deposit the entire compensation amount with accrued - 16 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:1042-DB C/W MFA.CROB No.100022 of 2021 interest before the Tribunal within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
e) On such deposit, out of the enhanced compensation amount, 1st claimant-wife of the deceased would be entitled to 50% and claimants No.2 and 3 shall be entitled to 25% each of the enhanced compensation.
 f) The amount in deposit, if any, be  transmitted to the concerned Tribunal forthwith along with original records.
g) Draw modified award accordingly.
